framework.name: NIST CSF
framework.blurb: Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 — the full set of 22 categories across Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover. Favoured by boards and US-aligned partners, mapped to ISO 27001 and Essential Eight so nothing is done twice.

subcategories.t: Organizational mission understood and informs cybersecurity risk management
Internal and external stakeholders and their expectations understood
Legal, regulatory and contractual cybersecurity requirements understood and managed
Critical objectives, capabilities and services that stakeholders depend on identified
Outcomes, capabilities and services the organisation depends on from others identified
Risk management objectives established and agreed by stakeholders
Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements established and communicated
Cybersecurity risk management activities integrated into enterprise risk management
Strategic direction describing appropriate risk responses established
Lines of communication for cybersecurity risk established across the organisation
Standardised method for calculating, documenting and prioritising risk established
Strategic opportunities (positive risks) characterised and included in risk discussions
Leadership accountable for cybersecurity risk, supported by a risk-aware culture
Cybersecurity roles, responsibilities and authorities established and communicated
Adequate resources allocated commensurate with the risk strategy
Cybersecurity included in human resources practices
Policy for managing cybersecurity risks established based on organisational context
Policy reviewed, updated and communicated to reflect changes
Risk management strategy outcomes reviewed to inform and adjust the strategy
Risk management performance evaluated and reviewed for adjustments needed
Organisational risk management performance evaluated against objectives, reported to leadership
Supply chain risk management program and strategy established and agreed by stakeholders
Cybersecurity roles for suppliers, customers and partners established and communicated
Supply chain risk management integrated into enterprise risk management and improvement processes
Suppliers known and prioritised by criticality
Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in the supply chain established and agreed
Planning and due diligence performed to reduce risk before entering a supplier relationship
Risks posed by suppliers, products and services monitored throughout the relationship
Relevant suppliers included in incident planning, response and recovery activities
Supply chain security practices integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk programs, monitored
Supply chain risk management plans include provisions for post-relationship activities (e.g. termination)
Inventories of hardware managed by the organisation maintained
Inventories of software and services managed by the organisation maintained
Representations of the organisation's authorised network communication and data flows maintained
Inventories of services provided by suppliers maintained
Assets prioritised based on classification, criticality and business value
Inventories of data and corresponding metadata maintained
Systems, hardware, software, services and data managed throughout their life cycles
Vulnerabilities in assets identified, validated and recorded
Cyber threat intelligence received from sharing forums and sources
Internal and external threats identified and recorded
Potential impacts and likelihoods of threats exploiting vulnerabilities identified and recorded
Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods and impacts used to determine and prioritise risk
Risk responses chosen, prioritised, planned, tracked and communicated
Changes and exceptions managed and evaluated as risk-affecting activities occur
Processes for receiving, analysing and responding to vulnerability disclosures established
Critical suppliers assessed prior to acquisition
Critical suppliers assessed via audits, test results, site visits or other evaluations
Improvements identified from evaluations
Improvements identified from security tests and exercises, including red-team/pen tests
Improvements identified from execution of operational processes, procedures and activities
Incident response and other cybersecurity plans affecting operations reviewed and updated
Identities and credentials for authorised users, services and hardware managed
Identities proofed and bound to credentials based on the context of interactions
Users, services and hardware authenticated
Identity assertions protected, conveyed and verified
Access permissions and authorisations managed per least privilege and separation of duties
Physical access to assets managed, protected and monitored
Personnel provided awareness and training to perform their cybersecurity-related tasks
Individuals in specialised roles provided awareness and training relevant to those roles
Confidentiality, integrity and availability of data-at-rest protected
Confidentiality, integrity and availability of data-in-transit protected
Confidentiality, integrity and availability of data-in-use protected
Backups of data created, protected, maintained and tested
Configuration management practices established and applied
Software maintained, replaced and removed commensurate with risk
Hardware maintained, replaced and removed commensurate with risk
Log records generated and made available for continuous monitoring
Installation and execution of unauthorised software prevented
Secure software development practices integrated and monitored throughout the life cycle
Networks and environments protected from unauthorised logical access and misuse
Technology assets protected from environmental threats
Mechanisms implemented to achieve resilience in normal and adverse situations
Adequate resource capacity maintained to ensure availability
Networks and network services monitored to find potentially adverse events
The physical environment monitored to find potentially adverse events
Personnel activity and technology usage monitored to find potentially adverse events
External service provider activities monitored to find potentially adverse events
Computing hardware, software and runtime environments monitored to find potentially adverse events
Potentially adverse events analysed to better understand associated activities
Information correlated from multiple sources
Estimated impact and scope of adverse events understood
Information on adverse events provided to authorised staff and tools
Cyber threat intelligence and other contextual information integrated into the analysis
Incidents declared when adverse events meet defined criteria
Incident response plan executed once an incident is declared, in coordination with stakeholders
Incident reports triaged and validated
Incidents categorised and prioritised
Incidents escalated or elevated as needed
Criteria for initiating incident recovery applied
Analysis performed to establish what took place during an incident and its root cause
Actions performed during an investigation recorded, integrity and provenance preserved
Incident data and metadata collected consistent with response plans
Incident magnitude estimated and validated
Internal and external stakeholders notified of incidents
Information shared with designated internal and external stakeholders
Incidents contained
Incidents eradicated
Recovery portion of the incident response plan activated
Recovery actions selected, scoped, prioritised and performed
Integrity of backups and restoration assets verified before use for recovery
Critical mission functions and cybersecurity risk management considered to establish post-recovery norms
Restoration performed and verified using approved procedures
Completion of the recovery process confirmed, normal operating status confirmed
Recovery activities and progress communicated to designated stakeholders
Public relations and reputation managed post-incident
